source.text: Καὶ διαγενομένου τοῦ σαββάτου Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ Σαλώμη ἠγόρασαν ἀρώματα ἵνα ἐλθοῦσαι ἀλείψωσιν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And having passed the Sabbath, Mary the Magdalene and Mary the [mother] of James and Salome bought spices so that having come they might anoint him.

en.L: And when the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene and Mary the [mother] of James and Salome bought spices so that they might come and anoint {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: After the Sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome purchased spices so that they could go and anoint {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body.
en.R: The Sabbath day ended. Then three women bought sweet-smelling spices: Mary from Magdala, Mary the mother of James, and Salome. They wanted to go and put them on Jesus' body.

vi.L: Và khi ngày Sa-bát đã qua, Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len, Ma-ri [mẹ] của Gia-cơ, và Sa-lô-mê mua hương liệu để đến xức cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Sau ngày Sa-bát, Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len, Ma-ri mẹ của Gia-cơ, và Sa-lô-mê mua hương liệu để đến xức thi thể {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Ngày Sa-bát đã qua. Bấy giờ có ba người phụ nữ đi mua hương liệu thơm: Ma-ri người làng Ma-đơ-la, Ma-ri mẹ của Gia-cơ, và Sa-lô-mê. Họ muốn đến xức hương liệu lên thi thể Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그리고 안식일이 지나자, 막달라 마리아와 야고보의 [어머니] 마리아와 살로메가 가서 그분께 바르려고 향료를 샀다.
ko.B: 안식일이 지나자, 막달라 마리아와 야고보의 어머니 마리아와 살로메는 가서 예수의 시신에 바르려고 향료를 샀다.
ko.R: 안식일이 끝났다. 그러자 세 여자가 좋은 냄새가 나는 향료를 샀다. 막달라 마리아, 야고보의 어머니 마리아, 그리고 살로메였다. 그들은 무덤에 가서 그 향료를 예수의 시신에 바르려고 했다.

es.L: Y pasado el sábado, María Magdalena y María la de Santiago y Salomé compraron aromas para ir a ungirlo.
es.B: Cuando terminó el sábado, María Magdalena, María la madre de Santiago, y Salomé compraron especias aromáticas para ir a ungir el cuerpo de Jesús.
es.R: Cuando terminó el sábado, tres mujeres compraron especias perfumadas: María, la de Magdala; María, la madre de Santiago; y Salomé. Querían ir a ponerlas sobre el cuerpo de Jesús.

fr.L: Et, le sabbat étant passé, Marie de Magdala, et Marie, la [mère] de Jacques, et Salomé achetèrent des aromates pour venir {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}oindre.
fr.B: Quand le sabbat fut passé, Marie de Magdala, Marie, mère de Jacques, et Salomé achetèrent des aromates pour aller oindre {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps.
fr.R: Quand le jour du sabbat a été terminé, trois femmes ont acheté des huiles parfumées : Marie de Magdala, Marie, la mère de Jacques, et Salomé. Elles voulaient aller les mettre sur le corps de Jésus.

sw.L: Na Sabato ilipokwisha, Mariamu Magdalene na Mariamu [mama] wa Yakobo na Salome walinunua manukato ili waje wampake.
sw.B: Sabato ilipopita, Mariamu Magdalene, Mariamu mama yake Yakobo, na Salome walinunua manukato ili waende kuupaka mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Siku ya Sabato ilipokwisha, wanawake watatu walinunua manukato yenye harufu nzuri: Mariamu wa Magdala, Mariamu mama yake Yakobo, na Salome. Walitaka kwenda kuupaka mwili wa Yesu.

pt.L: E, passado o sábado, Maria Madalena, e Maria, a [mãe] de Tiago, e Salomé compraram especiarias aromáticas para irem ungi-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}.
pt.B: Passado o sábado, Maria Madalena, Maria, mãe de Tiago, e Salomé compraram especiarias aromáticas para ir ungir o corpo {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.
pt.R: O sábado terminou. Então três mulheres compraram especiarias de cheiro agradável: Maria, da cidade de Magdala, Maria, a mãe de Tiago, e Salomé. Elas queriam ir passar as especiarias no corpo de Jesus.

am.L: ሰንበትም ካለፈ በኋላ መግደላዊት ማርያምና የያዕቆብ [እናት] ማርያም ሰሎሜም መጥተው ይቀቡት ዘንድ ሽቶ ገዙ።
am.B: ሰንበት ካለፈ በኋላ መግደላዊት ማርያም፣ የያዕቆብ እናት ማርያምና ሰሎሜ ሄደው ሥጋውን ለመቀባት ሽቶ ገዙ።
am.R: የሰንበት ቀን አለቀ። ከዚያም ሦስት ሴቶች ጥሩ መዓዛ ያለው ሽቶ ገዙ፤ እነርሱም ከመቅደላ የሆነችው ማርያም፣ የያዕቆብ እናት ማርያምና ሰሎሜ ነበሩ። ሄደው በኢየሱስ አስከሬን ላይ ሽቶውን ሊቀቡ ፈለጉ።

decisions.choice: when the Sabbath was over: after sunset on Saturday, when the Sabbath ended and shops could open
decisions.reason: The Jewish day ended at sunset. Jesus died on the day before the Sabbath (15:42), so the women could buy spices only on Saturday evening.

decisions.choice: Mary of James: the mother of James, as in 15:40
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "Mary of James". Mark 15:40 names her as the mother of James the younger and of Joses.

decisions.choice: spices to anoint him: fragrant oils poured on a body as a last honor
decisions.reason: Jews did not embalm. Spiced oils honored the dead and masked the smell of decay. Jesus had been buried in haste (15:46), and he had said that the woman at Bethany anointed his body beforehand for burial (14:8).

decisions.choice: Mary Magdalene: Mary from Magdala, a town on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: She watched the crucifixion and the burial (15:40, 15:47).

decisions.choice: his body (B); Jesus' body (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the women came to honor a dead body. Readable also says "from Magdala" and "sweet-smelling" to explain the name and the spices.

decisions.choice: "xức" for anointing the body
decisions.reason: "xức" is the Bible word for anointing and fits a last honour to the dead; "ướp" would suggest embalming, which the meaning decision does not describe.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서", "그분" and -시-, and Mark's historic presents stay present only at Literal ("간다", "본다", "말한다", 16:2-6), through chapter 16
alternatives: deity_pronoun spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7); "친히" carries the English "himself" in 16:8.

decisions.choice: "향료" for aromata; "바르다" for aleipho
decisions.reason: Fragrant oils put on a body as a last honour (meaning decision); "향료" is the word of the Korean John 19:40, and "바르다" is what one does with them on a body.

decisions.choice: aromas (L); especias aromáticas (B); especias perfumadas (R); ungir (L, B)
decisions.reason: The fragrant spices of a last honor to the dead (meaning decision m3). Literal uses "aromas", the word of John 19:40 Spanish; Balanced and Readable say what they were. "María la de Santiago" in Literal is the Spanish way of naming a woman by her family, as in 15:47 (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: el cuerpo de Jesús (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the anointing was for his dead body.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping Mark's present tense ("elles viennent" 16:2, "elles voient" 16:4, "il leur dit" 16:6); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the passage (16:1-20). The passé simple ("achetèrent", "s'enfuirent") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal uses it for the Greek past tenses and keeps the present where Mark tells a past event in the present, as the English Literal does. Readable uses the passé composé ("elles ont acheté"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first.

decisions.choice: des aromates, oindre (L, B); des huiles parfumées, les mettre sur le corps (R)
decisions.reason: "Aromates" is the French word for the fragrant substances used to honor the dead, as in French John 19:40; "épices" suggests cooking, and "embaumer" suggests preserving a body, which is not what the women meant to do (meaning decision m3). Readable says what the spices were and what the women would do with them.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal ("wanakuja" 16:2, "wanaona" 16:4, "anawaambia" 16:6); narrative past with -li- and -ka- at Balanced and Readable; deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives
decisions.reason: Mark tells the morning at the tomb partly in the present (meaning decisions at 16:2, 16:4). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as written Swahili narrative does. Swahili carries most pronouns inside the verb ("wampake", "mtamwona"), where no capital can be shown, so the reader setting appears only on free pronouns and possessives ("wake", "naye", "langu"). This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: manukato
decisions.reason: "Manukato" are fragrant spices and ointments, the word Swahili John 19:40 uses for the burial spices; "marashi" is perfume for the living. Readable adds "yenye harufu nzuri" (sweet-smelling), as the English does.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic
alternatives: Marking pronouns for Jesus in some other way
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Jesus in English has nothing to change in Amharic; most such pronouns are verb suffixes in any case (ይቀቡት "they might anoint him"). This holds for Mark 16.

decisions.choice: "ሽቶ" (perfume, fragrant ointment) for the spices
decisions.reason: The spices were fragrant oils and ointments for the body; "ቅመም" in Amharic is mostly a cooking spice, while "ሽቶ" is something fragrant put on the body.

source.text: καὶ λίαν πρωῒ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ἔρχονται ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον ἀνατείλαντος τοῦ ἡλίου.

records.literal_gloss: And very early on the first [day] of the week they come to the tomb, having risen the sun.

en.L: And very early on the first [day] of the week they come to the tomb, when the sun had risen.
en.B: On the first day of the week, very early, when the sun had come up, they came to the tomb.
en.R: Very early on Sunday morning, just after the sun came up, they went to the tomb.

vi.L: Và rất sớm vào ngày thứ nhất trong tuần, họ đến mộ, khi mặt trời đã mọc.
vi.B: Vào ngày thứ nhất trong tuần, rất sớm, lúc mặt trời vừa mọc, họ đến mộ.
vi.R: Sáng sớm Chủ Nhật, khi mặt trời vừa mọc, họ đi đến mộ.

ko.L: 그리고 주간의 첫 [날] 매우 이른 아침, 해가 돋았을 때에 그들이 무덤으로 간다.
ko.B: 주간의 첫날 아주 이른 아침, 해가 떠오를 무렵에 그들은 무덤으로 갔다.
ko.R: 일주일의 첫날인 일요일 아주 이른 아침이었다. 해가 막 떠오를 때 여자들은 무덤으로 갔다.

es.L: Y muy de mañana, el primer [día] de la semana, vienen al sepulcro, salido ya el sol.
es.B: El primer día de la semana, muy temprano, apenas salió el sol, fueron al sepulcro.
es.R: El domingo, muy temprano, cuando acababa de salir el sol, fueron a la tumba.

fr.L: Et, de très grand matin, le premier [jour] de la semaine, elles viennent au tombeau, le soleil s’étant levé.
fr.B: Le premier jour de la semaine, très tôt, alors que le soleil venait de se lever, elles se rendirent au tombeau.
fr.R: Le dimanche, très tôt le matin, juste après le lever du soleil, elles sont allées au tombeau.

sw.L: Na mapema sana siku ya kwanza ya juma wanakuja kaburini, jua likiwa limekwisha kuchomoza.
sw.B: Siku ya kwanza ya juma, mapema sana, jua lilipokuwa limechomoza, walikwenda kaburini.
sw.R: Jumapili asubuhi na mapema, mara tu baada ya jua kuchomoza, walikwenda kaburini.

pt.L: E muito cedo, no primeiro [dia] da semana, elas vão ao sepulcro, quando o sol já tinha nascido.
pt.B: No primeiro dia da semana, bem cedo, quando o sol já tinha nascido, elas foram ao sepulcro.
pt.R: Bem cedo no domingo de manhã, logo depois que o sol nasceu, elas foram ao túmulo.

am.L: በሳምንቱም የመጀመሪያ [ቀን] እጅግ ማለዳ ፀሐይ በወጣ ጊዜ ወደ መቃብሩ ይመጣሉ።
am.B: በሳምንቱ የመጀመሪያ ቀን በጣም ማለዳ፣ ፀሐይ እንደ ወጣች፣ ወደ መቃብሩ መጡ።
am.R: እሑድ ጠዋት በጣም ማለዳ፣ ፀሐይ ገና እንደ ወጣች፣ ወደ መቃብሩ ሄዱ።

decisions.choice: the first day of the week: Sunday, the day after the Sabbath
alternatives: the first day of a feast
decisions.reason: The Jewish week ended with the Sabbath, so the next day was the first day of the week. Christians later met on this day because Jesus rose on it.

decisions.choice: they come: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, past events are told in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: they came.

decisions.choice: very early, when the sun had risen: at dawn, as the sun was coming up
decisions.reason: "Very early" and "the sun having risen" together point to the first light of day.

decisions.choice: Sunday morning
alternatives: the first day of the week
decisions.reason: Readable names the day for readers who do not know the Jewish week.

decisions.choice: "Chủ Nhật" (R); "ngày thứ nhất trong tuần" (L, B)
alternatives: "ngày thứ nhất trong tuần" at R
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Jewish way of counting, as in John 20:1; Readable names the day as Vietnamese readers know it, as the English Readable says "Sunday".

decisions.choice: "주간의 첫 [날]" (L); "주간의 첫날" (B); "일주일의 첫날인 일요일" (R)
decisions.reason: The forms of the Korean John 20:1; Readable also names the day, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (vienen, ven, dice); pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Mark often tells his story in the present tense (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past, as Spanish stories are told. This applies to every such verb in the chapter (16:4, 16:6).

decisions.choice: El domingo (R); sepulcro (L, B); tumba (R)
alternatives: el primer día de la semana (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: As in English: the first day of the week is Sunday (meaning decision m1). "Sepulcro" and "tumba" as in 15:46 and John 20:1 Spanish.

decisions.choice: siku ya kwanza ya juma (L, B); Jumapili (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "siku ya kwanza ya juma", as Swahili John 20:1, so the Gospels match; Readable names the day, "Jumapili" (Sunday), as the English Readable does (meaning decision).

source.text: καὶ ἔλεγον πρὸς ἑαυτάς· Τίς ἀποκυλίσει ἡμῖν τὸν λίθον ἐκ τῆς θύρας τοῦ μνημείου;

records.literal_gloss: And they were saying to themselves, Who will roll away for us the stone from the door of the tomb?

en.L: And they were saying to one another, "Who will roll away the stone from the door of the tomb for us?"
en.B: They had been asking each other, "Who is going to roll the stone back from the entrance to the tomb for us?"
en.R: On the way they kept asking each other, "Who will move the stone away from the opening of the tomb for us?"

vi.L: Và họ cứ nói với nhau: "Ai sẽ lăn tảng đá khỏi cửa mộ cho chúng ta?"
vi.B: Họ đã hỏi nhau: "Ai sẽ lăn tảng đá ra khỏi cửa mộ giùm chúng ta đây?"
vi.R: Trên đường đi, họ cứ hỏi nhau: "Ai sẽ lăn tảng đá khỏi lối vào mộ cho chúng ta?"

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 서로 말하고 있었다. "누가 우리를 위해 무덤 문에서 그 돌을 굴려 내 줄까?"
ko.B: 그들은 가면서 서로 말했다. "누가 무덤 입구에서 그 돌을 굴려 내 줄까?"
ko.R: 여자들은 가는 길에 서로 계속 물었다. "누가 무덤 입구를 막고 있는 돌을 치워 줄까?"

es.L: Y decían entre sí: «¿Quién nos correrá la piedra de la puerta del sepulcro?».
es.B: Se preguntaban unas a otras: «¿Quién nos va a correr la piedra de la entrada del sepulcro?».
es.R: Por el camino se preguntaban unas a otras: «¿Quién nos va a quitar la piedra de la entrada de la tumba?».

fr.L: Et elles se disaient entre elles : « Qui nous roulera la pierre [loin] de la porte du tombeau ? »
fr.B: Elles se demandaient entre elles : « Qui va rouler pour nous la pierre qui ferme l’entrée du tombeau ? »
fr.R: En chemin, elles n’arrêtaient pas de se demander : « Qui va enlever pour nous la pierre qui ferme l’ouverture du tombeau ? »

sw.L: Nao walikuwa wakiambiana, "Nani atatuvingirishia lile jiwe kutoka mlangoni pa kaburi?"
sw.B: Walikuwa wakiulizana, "Ni nani atakayetuondolea jiwe kwenye mlango wa kaburi?"
sw.R: Njiani waliendelea kuulizana, "Nani atatusogezea jiwe kutoka kwenye mlango wa kaburi?"

pt.L: E diziam umas às outras: "Quem nos rolará a pedra da porta do sepulcro?"
pt.B: Elas vinham perguntando umas às outras: "Quem vai tirar para nós a pedra da entrada do sepulcro?"
pt.R: No caminho, elas ficavam perguntando umas às outras: "Quem vai tirar a pedra da entrada do túmulo para nós?"

am.L: እርስ በርሳቸውም፦ «ድንጋዩን ከመቃብሩ ደጃፍ ማን ያንከባልልናል?» ይባባሉ ነበር።
am.B: እርስ በርሳቸውም፦ «ድንጋዩን ከመቃብሩ መግቢያ ማን ያንከባልልናል?» እያሉ ይጠያየቁ ነበር።
am.R: በመንገድ ላይም፦ «ድንጋዩን ከመቃብሩ በር ላይ ማን ያነሣልናል?» እያሉ እርስ በርሳቸው ይጠያየቁ ነበር።

decisions.choice: the stone at the door: a large stone that closed the opening of a tomb cut in rock
alternatives: a small stone marking the grave
decisions.reason: Joseph had rolled such a stone against the entrance (15:46). It took several men to move.

decisions.choice: they were saying: they kept asking as they went
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous: it was their worry all the way to the tomb.

decisions.choice: On the way they kept asking
decisions.reason: Readable sets the question on the road to the tomb, as the continuous verb implies.

decisions.choice: correr la piedra (L, B); quitar la piedra (R)
decisions.reason: "Correr" a stone is the everyday Spanish for sliding it aside, which is what rolling it away from the opening meant (meaning decision m1); Readable says "quitar". "Unas a otras" is feminine, since the speakers are the three women.

decisions.choice: Por el camino (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the imperfect shows they kept asking as they went (meaning decision m2).

source.text: καὶ ἀναβλέψασαι θεωροῦσιν ὅτι ἀποκεκύλισται ὁ λίθος, ἦν γὰρ μέγας σφόδρα.

records.literal_gloss: And having looked up they see that has been rolled away the stone; it was for large extremely.

en.L: And looking up, they see that the stone has been rolled away; for it was extremely large.
en.B: When they looked up, they could see the stone had already been rolled away, and it was a huge stone.
en.R: But then they looked up and saw that the stone had been moved away already. And it was a very big stone!

vi.L: Và ngước mắt lên, họ thấy tảng đá đã được lăn đi rồi; vì tảng đá ấy rất lớn.
vi.B: Khi ngước lên, họ thấy tảng đá đã được lăn đi rồi; đó là một tảng đá rất to.
vi.R: Nhưng khi nhìn lên, họ thấy tảng đá đã được lăn đi rồi. Đó là một tảng đá rất lớn!

ko.L: 그런데 그들이 눈을 들어, 그 돌이 굴려져 있는 것을 본다. 그 돌은 매우 컸기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그런데 눈을 들어 보니, 돌은 이미 굴려져 있었다. 그것은 아주 큰 돌이었다.
ko.R: 그런데 여자들이 고개를 들어 보니, 그 돌이 벌써 옆으로 굴려져 있었다. 그 돌은 정말 큰 돌이었다!

es.L: Y al levantar la vista, ven que la piedra ha sido corrida; porque era sumamente grande.
es.B: Pero al levantar la vista, vieron que ya habían corrido la piedra, que era muy grande.
es.R: Pero cuando miraron, vieron que ya habían quitado la piedra. ¡Y era una piedra enorme!

fr.L: Et, levant les yeux, elles voient que la pierre a été roulée ; car elle était extrêmement grande.
fr.B: En levant les yeux, elles virent que la pierre avait déjà été roulée de côté. Or c’était une pierre énorme.
fr.R: Mais elles ont levé les yeux et elles ont vu que la pierre avait déjà été déplacée. Et c’était une très grosse pierre !

sw.L: Na walipotazama juu, wanaona kwamba jiwe limekwisha kuvingirishwa; kwa maana lilikuwa kubwa mno.
sw.B: Walipotazama, waliona kwamba jiwe lilikuwa limekwisha kuvingirishwa, nalo lilikuwa jiwe kubwa sana.
sw.R: Lakini walipoinua macho, waliona kwamba jiwe lilikuwa limekwisha kusogezwa. Na lilikuwa jiwe kubwa mno!

pt.L: E, levantando os olhos, veem que a pedra foi rolada para o lado; pois era muito grande.
pt.B: Quando ergueram os olhos, viram que a pedra já tinha sido rolada para o lado, e era uma pedra enorme.
pt.R: Mas então elas olharam e viram que a pedra já tinha sido tirada do lugar. E era uma pedra muito grande!

am.L: ቀና ብለውም ሲመለከቱ ድንጋዩ እንደ ተንከባለለ ያያሉ፤ እጅግ ትልቅ ነበርና።
am.B: ቀና ብለው ሲያዩ ድንጋዩ ቀድሞ ተንከባሎ ነበር፤ ድንጋዩም እጅግ ትልቅ ነበር።
am.R: ነገር ግን ቀና ብለው ሲያዩ ድንጋዩ ቀድሞውኑ ከቦታው ተንከባሎ ነበር። ድንጋዩም በጣም ትልቅ ነበር!

decisions.choice: for it was extremely large: explains their worry and why they could see from a distance that it had been moved
decisions.reason: Mark adds the note after the event. It looks back to the question of 16:3 and makes the opening of the tomb more striking.

decisions.choice: has been rolled away: a passive that does not name who moved it
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who rolled the stone. The passive leaves it to God's action, as the young man inside makes clear.

decisions.choice: rolled away, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have a related verb meaning rolled back or rolled up. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: they see: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: The sense is past, as in 16:2.

decisions.choice: ya habían corrido (B); ya habían quitado (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the passive; Balanced and Readable use the Spanish impersonal plural, which also names no one (meaning decision m2), as John 20:1 Spanish does. Literal keeps Mark's present "ven" and the "porque" that explains their worry (meaning decision m1).

source.text: καὶ εἰσελθοῦσαι εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον εἶδον νεανίσκον καθήμενον ἐν τοῖς δεξιοῖς περιβεβλημένον στολὴν λευκήν, καὶ ἐξεθαμβήθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having entered into the tomb they saw a young man sitting on the right, clothed in a robe white, and they were greatly amazed.

en.L: And entering into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a white robe, and they were utterly amazed.
en.B: On entering the tomb they found a young man seated on the right, wearing a white robe, and they were stunned.
en.R: They went into the tomb. A young man in a white robe was sitting there on the right side. The women were shocked and frightened.

vi.L: Và vào trong mộ, họ thấy một thanh niên ngồi ở bên phải, mặc áo choàng trắng, và họ vô cùng kinh ngạc.
vi.B: Bước vào trong mộ, họ thấy một thanh niên mặc áo choàng trắng ngồi ở phía bên phải, và họ hoảng hốt.
vi.R: Họ đi vào trong mộ. Có một thanh niên mặc áo choàng trắng đang ngồi ở phía bên phải. Các bà vừa sửng sốt vừa sợ hãi.

ko.L: 그리고 무덤 안으로 들어가서, 흰옷을 입은 한 청년이 오른쪽에 앉아 있는 것을 보고 몹시 놀랐다.
ko.B: 무덤 안으로 들어가 보니, 흰옷을 입은 청년 하나가 오른쪽에 앉아 있었다. 그들은 몹시 놀랐다.
ko.R: 여자들은 무덤 안으로 들어갔다. 그런데 흰옷을 입은 젊은 남자가 오른쪽에 앉아 있었다. 여자들은 깜짝 놀라고 무서웠다.

es.L: Y entrando en el sepulcro, vieron a un joven sentado a la derecha, vestido con una ropa larga blanca, y se espantaron.
es.B: Al entrar en el sepulcro, vieron a un joven sentado a la derecha, vestido con una ropa larga blanca, y se quedaron espantadas.
es.R: Entraron en la tumba. Allí, sentado al lado derecho, vieron a un joven con una ropa larga y blanca. Las mujeres se quedaron asombradas y llenas de miedo.

fr.L: Et, entrant dans le tombeau, elles virent un jeune homme assis à droite, vêtu d’une robe blanche, et elles furent saisies de stupeur.
fr.B: En entrant dans le tombeau, elles trouvèrent un jeune homme assis à droite, vêtu d’une longue robe blanche, et elles furent bouleversées.
fr.R: Elles sont entrées dans le tombeau. Un jeune homme habillé d’une longue robe blanche était assis là, sur le côté droit. Les femmes ont été bouleversées et effrayées.

sw.L: Na walipoingia kaburini, walimwona kijana mmoja ameketi upande wa kulia, amevaa vazi jeupe, nao wakastaajabu sana.
sw.B: Walipoingia ndani ya kaburi, walimkuta kijana ameketi upande wa kulia, amevaa vazi jeupe, wakashtuka mno.
sw.R: Waliingia ndani ya kaburi. Kijana mmoja aliyevaa vazi jeupe alikuwa ameketi pale upande wa kulia. Wanawake hao walishtuka na kuogopa.

pt.L: E, entrando no sepulcro, viram um jovem sentado do lado direito, vestido com uma túnica branca, e ficaram tomadas de espanto.
pt.B: Ao entrar no sepulcro, encontraram um jovem sentado à direita, vestido com uma túnica branca, e ficaram atônitas.
pt.R: Elas entraram no túmulo. Um jovem vestido com uma túnica branca estava sentado ali, do lado direito. As mulheres ficaram assustadas e com medo.

am.L: ወደ መቃብሩም ገብተው ነጭ ልብስ የለበሰ ወጣት በቀኝ በኩል ተቀምጦ አዩ፤ እጅግም ደነገጡ።
am.B: ወደ መቃብሩ ሲገቡ ነጭ ልብስ የለበሰ አንድ ወጣት በቀኝ በኩል ተቀምጦ አገኙ፤ በጣም ደነገጡም።
am.R: ወደ መቃብሩ ውስጥ ገቡ። ነጭ ልብስ የለበሰ አንድ ወጣት በቀኝ በኩል ተቀምጦ ነበር። ሴቶቹም ደነገጡ፤ ፈሩም።

decisions.choice: a young man in a white robe: a messenger from God
alternatives: the young man who fled in 14:51-52
decisions.reason: White clothing marks heavenly beings (9:3; Daniel 7:9). Matthew 28:2-5 calls him an angel of the Lord, and Luke 24:4 speaks of two men in shining clothes. Mark says only "a young man"; some have linked him with the young man who fled in 14:51, but Mark does not.

decisions.choice: utterly amazed: overcome with awe and alarm
decisions.reason: The verb is strong. It is used of the crowd at 9:15 and of Jesus' distress in Gethsemane (14:33). Here it is fear and awe at once.

decisions.choice: on the right: the right side of the tomb as one enters
decisions.reason: A tomb cut in rock had a ledge or bench where the body was laid. The young man sits inside, to the right.

decisions.choice: shocked and frightened
decisions.reason: Readable gives both sides of the strong verb, which joins awe and alarm.

decisions.choice: "áo choàng trắng"
decisions.reason: "áo dài" today names the Vietnamese national dress (see John 19:23); "áo choàng" is a long outer robe.

decisions.choice: "청년" (L, B); "젊은 남자" (R)
decisions.reason: Mark says "a young man" and leaves the reader to see a messenger from God (meaning decision); Korean keeps his word rather than naming an angel.

decisions.choice: se espantaron (L); se quedaron espantadas (B); se quedaron asombradas y llenas de miedo (R)
decisions.reason: The verb joins awe and alarm (meaning decision m2): Spanish "espantarse" carries both. Readable names both. The same verb in 16:6 is rendered with the same words where Spanish allows.

decisions.choice: una ropa larga blanca
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a long robe; "túnica" and "manto" are kept for the other garments of John 19 and Mark 15.

decisions.choice: saisies de stupeur (L); bouleversées (B); bouleversées et effrayées (R); the same verb in 16:6
decisions.reason: The verb joins awe and alarm (meaning decision m2): "épouvantées" says only fear and "étonnées" only surprise. Each level uses the same wording again when the young man tells them not to feel this way (16:6), so that the reader hears the echo.

decisions.choice: kijana at every level
decisions.reason: Mark says "a young man"; the meaning note says he is God's messenger, but the text does not use the word "angel", so no level says "malaika".

source.text: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐταῖς· Μὴ ἐκθαμβεῖσθε· Ἰησοῦν ζητεῖτε τὸν Ναζαρηνὸν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον· ἠγέρθη, οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε· ἴδε ὁ τόπος ὅπου ἔθηκαν αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: He but says to them, Not be amazed; Jesus you seek the Nazarene, the [one] having been crucified; he was raised, not he is here; see the place where they laid him;

en.L: But he says to them, "Do not be amazed. You are seeking Jesus the Nazarene, the one who has been crucified. He has been raised; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is not here. See the place where they laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: But he told them, "Do not be alarmed. You have come looking for Jesus from Nazareth, the one who was crucified. He has been raised; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is not here. Look, this is the place where they laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: But he told them, "Do not be frightened. You are looking for Jesus from Nazareth, who was killed on a cross. God has raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from death! He is not here. Look, here is the place where they put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body.

vi.L: Người ấy nói với họ: "Đừng kinh ngạc. Các bà tìm Đức Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét, Đấng đã bị đóng đinh. Ngài đã được làm cho sống lại; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không ở đây. Hãy xem chỗ người ta đã đặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Nhưng người ấy bảo họ: "Đừng hoảng sợ. Các bà đến tìm Đức Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét, Đấng đã bị đóng đinh. Ngài đã được làm cho sống lại; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không còn ở đây. Kìa, đây là chỗ người ta đã đặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Nhưng người ấy nói với họ: "Đừng sợ. Các bà đang tìm Đức Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét, Đấng đã bị đóng đinh trên cây thập tự. Đức Chúa Trời đã khiến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sống lại từ cõi chết! Ngài không có ở đây. Hãy nhìn xem, đây là chỗ người ta đã đặt thi thể của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그러자 그가 그들에게 말한다. "놀라지 마라. 너희는 십자가에 못 박히신 나사렛 사람 예수를 찾고 있다. 그분은 살아나셨다. 여기에 계시지 않는다. 보아라, 그들이 그분을 모셨던 곳이다.
ko.B: 청년이 그들에게 말했다. "놀라지 마라. 너희는 십자가에 못 박히신 나사렛 예수를 찾고 있구나. 그분은 살아나셨다. 여기에 계시지 않는다. 보아라, 여기가 그분을 모셨던 곳이다.
ko.R: 그러나 청년이 말했다. "무서워하지 마라. 너희는 십자가에 못 박혀 돌아가신 나사렛 예수를 찾고 있구나. 하나님께서 그분을 죽음에서 다시 살리셨다! 그분은 여기 계시지 않는다. 보아라, 여기가 그분의 시신을 모셨던 곳이다.

es.L: Pero él les dice: «{{plural_you:No se espanten|No os espantéis}}. {{plural_you:Buscan|Buscáis}} a Jesús el Nazareno, el crucificado. Ha sido resucitado; no está aquí. {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} el lugar donde {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} pusieron.
es.B: Pero él les dijo: «{{plural_you:No se asusten|No os asustéis}}. {{plural_you:Buscan|Buscáis}} a Jesús de Nazaret, el que fue crucificado. Ha sido resucitado; no está aquí. {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, este es el lugar donde {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} pusieron.
es.R: Pero él les dijo: «{{plural_you:No tengan miedo|No tengáis miedo}}. {{plural_you:Están buscando|Estáis buscando}} a Jesús de Nazaret, al que clavaron en una cruz. ¡Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha resucitado! No está aquí. {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, aquí es donde pusieron {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cuerpo.

fr.L: Mais lui leur dit : « Ne soyez pas saisies de stupeur. Vous cherchez Jésus le Nazarénien, le crucifié. Il a été ressuscité ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’est pas ici. Voyez le lieu où ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avaient déposé.
fr.B: Mais il leur dit : « Ne soyez pas bouleversées. Vous cherchez Jésus de Nazareth, celui qui a été crucifié. Il a été ressuscité ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’est pas ici. Regardez, voici l’endroit où on {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avait déposé.
fr.R: Mais il leur a dit : « N’ayez pas peur. Vous cherchez Jésus de Nazareth, celui qui a été cloué sur une croix. Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a ressuscité ! Il n’est pas ici. Regardez, voici l’endroit où on avait déposé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps.

sw.L: Lakini yeye anawaambia, "Msishtuke. Mnamtafuta Yesu Mnazareti, yule ambaye amesulubiwa. Amefufuliwa; hayuko hapa. Tazameni mahali walipomlaza.
sw.B: Lakini yeye akawaambia, "Msitishike. Mnamtafuta Yesu wa Nazareti, aliyesulubiwa. Amefufuliwa; hayuko hapa. Angalieni, hapa ndipo mahali walipomlaza.
sw.R: Lakini aliwaambia, "Msiogope. Mnamtafuta Yesu kutoka Nazareti, aliyeuawa msalabani. Mungu amemfufua kutoka kwa wafu! Hayuko hapa. Angalieni, hapa ndipo walipouweka mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

pt.L: Mas ele lhes diz: "Não se espantem. Vocês procuram Jesus, o nazareno, o que foi crucificado. Ele foi ressuscitado; {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} não está aqui. Vejam o lugar onde {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} puseram.
pt.B: Mas ele lhes disse: "Não fiquem assustadas. Vocês vieram procurar Jesus de Nazaré, aquele que foi crucificado. Ele foi ressuscitado; {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} não está aqui. Vejam, este é o lugar onde {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} puseram.
pt.R: Mas ele disse a elas: "Não tenham medo. Vocês estão procurando Jesus de Nazaré, que foi morto numa cruz. Deus {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} ressuscitou! Ele não está aqui. Olhem, aqui é o lugar onde puseram o corpo {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.

am.L: እርሱም እንዲህ ይላቸዋል፦ «አትደንግጡ፤ የተሰቀለውን ናዝራዊውን ኢየሱስን ትፈልጋላችሁ፤ ተነሥቷል፤ እዚህ የለም፤ ያኖሩበትን ስፍራ እዩ።
am.B: እርሱ ግን እንዲህ አላቸው፦ «አትደንግጡ። የተሰቀለውን የናዝሬቱን ኢየሱስን ልትፈልጉ መጥታችኋል። ተነሥቷል፤ እዚህ የለም። ተመልከቱ፤ ያኖሩበት ስፍራ ይህ ነው።
am.R: እርሱ ግን እንዲህ አላቸው፦ «አትፍሩ። በመስቀል ላይ የተገደለውን የናዝሬቱን ኢየሱስን ትፈልጋላችሁ። እግዚአብሔር ከሞት አስነሥቶታል! እዚህ የለም። እዩ፤ አስከሬኑን ያኖሩበት ቦታ ይህ ነው።

decisions.choice: he has been raised: a passive, God raised him
alternatives: he has risen by his own power
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed, a common way of speaking of God's action. Jesus spoke of being raised in 14:28.

decisions.choice: the one who has been crucified: a perfect participle, the crucified one
alternatives: the one who was once crucified and is no longer
decisions.reason: The form describes him by what happened to him and what it made him: he is still the crucified one, now raised.

decisions.choice: the Nazarene: the man from Nazareth
alternatives: a member of a group called Nazarenes
decisions.reason: The word names Jesus by his hometown in Galilee (1:9, 1:24, 14:67).

decisions.choice: see the place: the empty ledge where the body had lain
decisions.reason: The women had watched where he was laid (15:47). The young man shows them the place, now empty.

decisions.choice: God has raised him from death; his body
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who raised him, as the passive implies, and says "from death". It also says "killed on a cross" for "crucified".

decisions.choice: the young man addresses the women as "các bà"
decisions.reason: A respectful, neutral address to grown women, as the angels say "bà" to Mary in John 20:13.

decisions.choice: "đã được làm cho sống lại" (L, B), keeping the passive; R "Đức Chúa Trời đã khiến ... sống lại"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the passive as God's act. "đã sống lại" alone would lose it; Readable names God, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: The young man speaks to the women in the plain style (해라체: "놀라지 마라") and honours Jesus ("못 박히신", "계시지 않는다")
decisions.reason: As the angels speak to Mary in the Korean John 20:13; a messenger from God speaks with authority.

decisions.choice: "살아나셨다" (L, B); "하나님께서 그분을 ... 다시 살리셨다" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek passive means that God raised him (meaning decision); Korean has no natural passive of "raise", so Literal and Balanced use the usual intransitive verb, and Readable names God as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: The young man speaks to the women as a group, so every plural "you" takes the reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), here and in 16:7 and 16:15-18. The verb forms are the same for vosotras.

decisions.choice: Ha sido resucitado (L, B); Dios lo ha resucitado (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is passive: God raised him (meaning decision m1). "Ha resucitado" would be correct Spanish but hides the passive, so Literal and Balanced keep it and Readable names God, as the English does.

decisions.choice: el Nazareno (L); de Nazaret (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of the word, Balanced and Readable say what it means, the man from Nazareth (meaning decision m3), as John 19:19 Spanish does.

decisions.choice: Il a été ressuscité (L, B); Dieu l'a ressuscité (R)
decisions.reason: The familiar French "Il est ressuscité" makes Jesus the subject of the verb; the Greek is a passive whose unnamed agent is God (meaning decision m1), so Literal and Balanced keep the passive and Readable names God, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: le Nazarénien, le crucifié (L); de Nazareth, celui qui a été crucifié (B, R)
decisions.reason: Mark's word is not the one John uses ("le Nazôréen" in French John 18:5), so Literal keeps a distinct form, "le Nazarénien"; Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m3). Literal "le crucifié" keeps the participle as a name for him (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Amefufuliwa (L, B); Mungu amemfufua (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is passive: God raised him (meaning decision). "Amefufuliwa" (he has been raised) keeps the passive; the familiar "amefufuka" (he has risen) would make Jesus the one who acted. Readable names God, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Mnazareti (L); wa Nazareti (B); kutoka Nazareti (R)
decisions.reason: As in Swahili John 18:5: "Mnazareti" is the ordinary word for a man of Nazareth and keeps it as a title at Literal; Balanced and Readable say where he came from.

decisions.choice: foi ressuscitado
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 28:6: Portuguese most often says "ressuscitou", which hides the passive that m1 notes (God raised him). Literal and Balanced keep "foi ressuscitado"; Readable names God, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ተነሥቷል" ("he has risen, been raised") (L, B); "እግዚአብሔር ከሞት አስነሥቶታል" ("God has raised him") (R)
decisions.reason: The Amharic passive-reflexive form covers both "he rose" and "he was raised", as the Greek passive is read here (meaning decision m1); Readable names God as the one who raised him, as the English Readable does (as Matthew 28:6).

decisions.choice: "ናዝራዊ" (the Nazarene) at Literal; "የናዝሬቱ" ("the one from Nazareth") at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek's title-like word; Balanced and Readable say plainly that he was the man from Nazareth (meaning decision m3).

source.text: ἀλλὰ ὑπάγετε εἴπατε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ Πέτρῳ ὅτι Προάγει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν· ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ὄψεσθε, καθὼς εἶπεν ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: But go, say to the disciples of him and to the Peter that he goes before you into the Galilee; there him you will see, as he said to you.

en.L: But go, tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and Peter that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is going ahead of you into Galilee; there you will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you."
en.B: But go and tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, and Peter too, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is going on ahead of you to Galilee. You will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} there, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to you."
en.R: Now go and tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, and be sure to tell Peter too. Tell them, 'Jesus is going to Galilee ahead of you. You will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} there, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you.'"

vi.L: Nhưng hãy đi, nói với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và với Phi-e-rơ rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi trước các ông đến Ga-li-lê; tại đó các ông sẽ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói với các ông."
vi.B: Nhưng hãy đi báo cho các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và cả Phi-e-rơ nữa, rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi trước các ông đến Ga-li-lê. Các ông sẽ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở đó, đúng như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói với các ông."
vi.R: Bây giờ hãy đi báo cho các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và nhớ báo cho cả Phi-e-rơ nữa. Hãy nói với họ: 'Đức Giê-xu đi trước các ông đến Ga-li-lê. Các ông sẽ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở đó, đúng như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói với các ông.'"

ko.L: 그러니 가서 그분의 제자들과 베드로에게, 그분이 너희보다 먼저 갈릴리로 가신다고 말하여라. 그분이 너희에게 말씀하신 대로, 너희가 거기서 그분을 뵐 것이다."
ko.B: 이제 가서 그분의 제자들과 베드로에게 전하여라. 그분이 너희보다 먼저 갈릴리로 가신다. 그분이 너희에게 말씀하신 대로, 너희는 거기서 그분을 뵐 것이다."
ko.R: 이제 가서 예수의 제자들에게 알려라. 베드로에게도 꼭 알려라. 이렇게 전하여라. '예수께서 너희보다 먼저 갈릴리로 가신다. 예수께서 전에 너희에게 말씀하신 대로, 너희는 거기서 그분을 뵙게 될 것이다.'"

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:vayan|id}}, {{plural_you:digan|decid}} a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y a Pedro que va delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a Galilea; allí {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:verán|veréis}}, como {{plural_you:les|os}} dijo».
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:vayan|id}} y {{plural_you:digan|decid}} a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, y también a Pedro, que va delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a Galilea. Allí {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:verán|veréis}}, tal como {{plural_you:les|os}} dijo».
es.R: Ahora {{plural_you:vayan|id}} y {{plural_you:díganselo|decídselo}} a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, y no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} de decírselo a Pedro: “Jesús va a Galilea antes que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Allí {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:verán|veréis}}, tal como {{plural_you:les|os}} dijo”».

fr.L: Mais allez, dites à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et à Pierre qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous précède en Galilée ; là, vous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} verrez, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous l’a dit. »
fr.B: Mais allez dire à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, et à Pierre aussi, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous précède en Galilée. C’est là que vous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} verrez, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous l’a dit. »
fr.R: Maintenant, allez le dire à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, et surtout n’oubliez pas Pierre. Dites-leur : “Jésus va en Galilée avant vous. C’est là que vous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} verrez, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous l’a dit.” »

sw.L: Lakini nendeni, mwaambieni wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na Petro kwamba anatangulia mbele yenu kwenda Galilaya; huko mtamwona, kama alivyowaambia."
sw.B: Basi nendeni mkawaambie wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na Petro pia, kwamba anatangulia mbele yenu kwenda Galilaya. Huko mtamwona, kama alivyowaambia."
sw.R: Sasa nendeni mkawaambie wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na hakikisheni mnamwambia Petro pia. Waambieni, 'Yesu anatangulia mbele yenu kwenda Galilaya. Mtamwona huko, kama alivyowaambia.'"

pt.L: Mas vão, digam aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos e a Pedro que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} vai adiante de vocês para a Galileia; lá vocês {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} verão, como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes disse."
pt.B: Mas vão e digam aos discípulos {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, e também a Pedro, que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} está indo adiante de vocês para a Galileia. Lá vocês {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} verão, como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes disse."
pt.R: Agora vão e digam aos seguidores {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, e não deixem de contar a Pedro também. Digam a eles: 'Jesus está indo para a Galileia antes de vocês. Lá vocês vão vê-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}, como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse a vocês.'"

am.L: ነገር ግን ሂዱ፤ ከእናንተ በፊት ወደ ገሊላ እንደሚሄድ፣ እንደ ነገራችሁም በዚያ እንደምታዩት ለደቀ መዛሙርቱና ለጴጥሮስ ንገሩ።»
am.B: ነገር ግን ሂዱና ከእናንተ በፊት ወደ ገሊላ እንደሚሄድ ለደቀ መዛሙርቱ፣ ለጴጥሮስም ደግሞ ንገሩ። እንደ ነገራችሁም በዚያ ታዩታላችሁ።»

decisions.choice: as he told you: Jesus' promise on the way to the Mount of Olives (14:28)
decisions.reason: In 14:28 Jesus said, "After I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee." The promise is now kept.

decisions.choice: and Peter: Peter is named because he had denied Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter denied Jesus three times (14:66-72). Naming him here shows that he is not shut out.

decisions.choice: goes before you: leads the way, as a shepherd before his flock
decisions.reason: In 14:27-28 the promise follows the saying about the scattered sheep. Jesus will gather them again in Galilee.

decisions.choice: that: introduces the message, which may be read as direct speech
decisions.reason: The word can mark a reported message or the words to be spoken. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: be sure to tell Peter; Tell them
alternatives: tell his disciples and Peter that
decisions.reason: Readable sets out the message as the women's own words and stresses that Peter is to hear it.

decisions.choice: "các ông" for the disciples in the message
decisions.reason: The "you" of the message is the disciples, to whom Jesus made the promise (14:28), not the women; Vietnamese must choose, and "các ông" names the men respectfully.

decisions.choice: "môn đồ" at every level
alternatives: "những người theo Ngài" (like the English Readable "followers")
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "môn đồ" at every level, Readable included; it is a plain, familiar word.

decisions.choice: "뵙다" for seeing Jesus
decisions.reason: The humble verb for meeting a superior, as in the Korean John 20:18; the messenger speaks of Jesus with honour.

decisions.choice: no dejen de decírselo a Pedro; the message as direct speech (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable shows why Peter is named (meaning decision m2) and gives the message as direct speech, which the Greek allows (meaning decision m4), with the inner quotation marks “ ”.

decisions.choice: va delante de ustedes (L, B); va ... antes que ustedes (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means going ahead, leading the way (meaning decision m3). The "you" includes the disciples, so the vosotros form is masculine.

decisions.choice: ses disciples (R)
decisions.reason: The French brief keeps "disciples" at every level, Readable included, as French John does; the word is plain enough in French, where the English Readable says "followers".

decisions.choice: wanafunzi at Readable
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "disciples", which the Swahili style guide keeps as "wanafunzi" at every level; the English Readable says "followers".

decisions.choice: "ደቀ መዛሙርት" (disciples) at Readable too, here and through 16:11-20
decisions.reason: "ደቀ መዛሙርት" is the everyday Amharic word for disciples and is kept at every level in the Amharic Gospels, where the English Readable says "followers".

source.text: καὶ ἐξελθοῦσαι ἔφυγον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου, εἶχεν γὰρ αὐτὰς τρόμος καὶ ἔκστασις· καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν εἶπαν, ἐφοβοῦντο γάρ.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out they fled from the tomb, had seized for them trembling and amazement; and to none nothing they said, they were afraid for.

en.L: And going out, they fled from the tomb, for trembling and amazement had seized them; and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.
en.B: They went out and ran from the tomb, trembling and beside themselves. And they told no one anything, for they were afraid.
en.R: The women went out and ran away from the tomb. They were shaking and could hardly think. They did not tell anyone anything, because they were afraid.

vi.L: Và đi ra, họ chạy trốn khỏi mộ, vì sự run rẩy và kinh ngạc đã xâm chiếm họ; và họ không nói gì với ai cả, vì họ sợ.
vi.B: Họ ra khỏi mộ và bỏ chạy, run rẩy và sững sờ. Họ không nói gì với ai cả, vì họ sợ hãi.
vi.R: Các bà đi ra và chạy trốn khỏi ngôi mộ. Họ run rẩy và hoảng hốt đến nỗi không nghĩ được gì. Họ không nói với ai điều gì cả, vì họ sợ.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 나가서 무덤에서 도망쳤다. 떨림과 놀라움이 그들을 사로잡았기 때문이다. 그리고 그들은 아무에게도 아무 말도 하지 않았다. 그들이 두려워했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 여자들은 무덤에서 나와 도망쳤다. 몸이 떨리고 넋이 나갔던 것이다. 그리고 아무에게도 아무 말을 하지 않았다. 두려웠기 때문이다.
ko.R: 여자들은 밖으로 나와서 무덤에서 달아났다. 몸이 덜덜 떨리고 정신이 하나도 없었다. 그들은 아무에게도 아무 말도 하지 않았다. 너무 무서웠기 때문이다.

es.L: Y saliendo, huyeron del sepulcro, porque temblor y espanto se habían apoderado de ellas; y no dijeron nada a nadie, porque tenían miedo.
es.B: Salieron y huyeron del sepulcro, temblando y fuera de sí. Y no le dijeron nada a nadie, porque tenían miedo.
es.R: Las mujeres salieron y se fueron corriendo de la tumba. Temblaban y estaban tan asombradas que casi no podían pensar. No le dijeron nada a nadie, porque tenían miedo.

fr.L: Et, étant sorties, elles s’enfuirent du tombeau, car le tremblement et le saisissement les tenaient ; et elles ne dirent rien à personne : elles avaient peur, en effet.
fr.B: Elles sortirent et s’enfuirent loin du tombeau, tremblantes et hors d’elles-mêmes. Et elles ne dirent rien à personne, car elles avaient peur.
fr.R: Les femmes sont sorties et se sont enfuies loin du tombeau. Elles tremblaient et elles étaient complètement bouleversées. Elles n’ont rien dit à personne, parce qu’elles avaient peur.

sw.L: Na walipotoka, walikimbia kutoka kaburini, kwa maana kutetemeka na mshangao vilikuwa vimewashika; wala hawakumwambia mtu yeyote neno lolote, kwa maana walikuwa wakiogopa.
sw.B: Wakatoka, wakakimbia kutoka kaburini, wakitetemeka na wakiwa wamechanganyikiwa. Hawakumwambia mtu yeyote chochote, kwa sababu waliogopa.

pt.L: E, saindo, fugiram do sepulcro, pois tremor e assombro as tinham tomado; e não disseram nada a ninguém, pois tinham medo.
pt.B: Elas saíram e fugiram do sepulcro, tremendo e fora de si. E não disseram nada a ninguém, porque estavam com medo.
pt.R: As mulheres saíram e fugiram do túmulo. Estavam tremendo e mal conseguiam pensar. Não contaram nada a ninguém, porque estavam com medo.

am.L: ወጥተውም ከመቃብሩ ሸሹ፤ መንቀጥቀጥና መደነቅ ይዞአቸው ነበርና፤ ለማንም ምንም አልተናገሩም፤ ይፈሩ ነበርና።
am.B: እነርሱም ወጥተው እየተንቀጠቀጡና እጅግ ተደናግጠው ከመቃብሩ ሸሹ። ለማንም ምንም አልነገሩም፤ ፈርተው ነበርና።
am.R: ሴቶቹ ወጥተው ከመቃብሩ ሮጠው ሄዱ። ይንቀጠቀጡ ነበር፤ ማሰብም አቃታቸው። ስለ ፈሩም ለማንም ምንም አልተናገሩም።

decisions.choice: the Gospel ends at 16:8 in the earliest manuscripts; the endings that follow are later additions, printed by the SBLGNT in double brackets
decisions.reason: The two oldest complete manuscripts of the New Testament, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, both from the fourth century, end Mark at 16:8 with "for they were afraid". Most manuscripts, nearly all of them later, go on with 16:9-20, the longer ending. Its style and vocabulary differ from the rest of Mark: many of its words occur nowhere else in the Gospel, it introduces Mary Magdalene in 16:9 as if she had not just been named in 16:1, and its appearances read like a summary of those told in Luke, John and Acts. Some manuscripts have instead a short ending after 16:8 (the women report briefly to Peter's companions, and Jesus sends out through them the proclamation of eternal salvation), and a few have the short ending followed by the longer one. The SBLGNT prints both endings after 16:8 in double brackets, which mark a passage that was not part of the original text but is old and widely read. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: an open question: Mark may have ended here on purpose, or his ending may have been lost
decisions.reason: Whether Mark meant to end at 16:8 or his first ending was lost is an open question. A book ending on the word "for", with the women silent and afraid, is very unusual, and it leaves the meeting promised in 16:7 untold. Some think the last page of the earliest copy was lost or never written. Others think Mark ended here on purpose: the promise of 16:7 stands, the reader knows the message was later told, and the silence leaves the reader facing the empty tomb. The later endings show that early copyists felt the Gospel needed a fuller close. The manuscripts cannot settle the question. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: for they were afraid: the Greek sentence ends with the word for
decisions.reason: A Greek sentence may end with "for", and short sentences like this one do occur. But no other book is known to end that way, which is part of the question about Mark's ending.

decisions.choice: trembling and amazement: shaking with fear and beside themselves with awe
decisions.reason: The second word means being out of oneself with astonishment, as in 5:42. Fear and awe are the response to God's power in Mark (4:41; 5:15).

decisions.choice: they said nothing to anyone: two negatives together, a strong statement
decisions.reason: Greek piles up negatives for emphasis. They told no one on the way. The message itself was later told, or the story would not be known.

decisions.choice: beside themselves (B); could hardly think (R)
decisions.reason: The word means being out of oneself. Balanced and Readable say so in plain words. Both keep "afraid" as the last word, as the Greek ends with fear.

decisions.choice: "vì họ sợ" at the end of the sentence
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence ends on the word "for"; Vietnamese cannot end on a conjunction, so Literal ends as close as it can, with "họ sợ" last. The meaning decision describes the abrupt ending.

decisions.choice: The last clause ends with "때문이다" at every level
alternatives: "그들은 두려워서 아무에게도 아무 말도 하지 않았다"
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence ends on the word "for" (meaning decision); Korean cannot end there, but keeping the reason as a separate final clause leaves the abrupt close on the women's fear, and "아무에게도 아무 말도" keeps the double negative.

decisions.choice: temblando y fuera de sí (B); temblaban ... casi no podían pensar (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the women shook with fear and were beside themselves with awe (meaning decision m4). "Espanto" in Literal is the noun of the verb used in 16:5.

decisions.choice: porque tenían miedo, at the end
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence ends with the word for "for" (meaning decision m3); Spanish cannot end on "porque", so every level ends with "tenían miedo", which keeps the fear as the last word. "No ... nada a nadie" keeps the strong double negative, natural in Spanish (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: elles avaient peur, en effet (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence, and the Gospel in the earliest manuscripts, ends with the word "for" (meaning decision m3). French cannot end on "car", but "en effet", which means the same, can stand last, so Literal keeps the abrupt explanatory ending; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary order.

decisions.choice: mshangao (L); wakiwa wamechanganyikiwa (B); hawakuweza kufikiri vizuri (R)
decisions.reason: The word is being beside oneself with awe (meaning decision). Literal says "mshangao" (amazement); Balanced "wamechanganyikiwa" (bewildered, beside themselves); Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: kwa maana walikuwa wakiogopa, last in the sentence
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence, and in the earliest manuscripts the Gospel, ends with the word "for" (meaning decision). Swahili cannot end on a conjunction, so Literal keeps "for they were afraid" as the last words, with the continuing past "walikuwa wakiogopa" for the Greek imperfect.

decisions.choice: medo as the last word
alternatives: pois estavam com medo, e não disseram nada
decisions.reason: As the English keeps "afraid" last: Mark's sentence, and in the earliest manuscripts his book, ends with fear (m1-m3), and Portuguese can end the sentence the same way at every level.

en.L: [And all the things commanded they reported briefly to those around Peter.
en.B: [They gave Peter and those with him a short report of all they had been told.
en.R: [The women quickly told Peter and the others with him everything the young man had told them to say.

vi.B: [Họ thuật lại vắn tắt cho Phi-e-rơ và những người ở với ông tất cả những gì họ đã được dặn bảo.
vi.R: [Các bà nhanh chóng kể lại cho Phi-e-rơ và những người ở với ông mọi điều người thanh niên đã dặn họ nói.

ko.L: [그리고 그들은 명령받은 모든 것을 베드로 주위에 있는 사람들에게 간략하게 알렸다.
ko.B: [여자들은 전하라고 들은 모든 것을 베드로와 그 일행에게 간단히 전했다.
ko.R: [여자들은 청년이 전하라고 한 말을 모두 베드로와 그와 함께 있던 사람들에게 간단히 전했다.

es.L: [Y todo lo que se les había mandado lo comunicaron brevemente a los que estaban con Pedro.
es.B: [Ellas les contaron brevemente a Pedro y a los que estaban con él todo lo que se les había encargado.
es.R: [En pocas palabras, las mujeres les contaron a Pedro y a los que estaban con él todo lo que el joven les había mandado decir.

fr.L: [Et toutes les choses prescrites, elles les rapportèrent brièvement à ceux qui étaient autour de Pierre.
fr.B: [Elles firent à Pierre et à ceux qui étaient avec lui un bref récit de tout ce qu’on leur avait dit.
fr.R: [Les femmes ont raconté en quelques mots à Pierre et aux autres qui étaient avec lui tout ce que le jeune homme leur avait dit de dire.

sw.L: [Na mambo yote waliyoagizwa waliwaeleza kwa ufupi wale waliokuwa pamoja na Petro.

sw.R: [Wanawake hao walimweleza Petro na wenzake kwa ufupi yote ambayo yule kijana aliwaagiza waseme.

pt.L: [E anunciaram brevemente aos que estavam com Pedro tudo o que lhes tinha sido ordenado.
pt.B: [Elas deram a Pedro e aos que estavam com ele um breve relato de tudo o que lhes tinha sido dito.
pt.R: [As mulheres logo contaram a Pedro e aos outros que estavam com ele tudo o que o jovem tinha mandado dizer.

decisions.reason: This ending is found in a few manuscripts, mostly after 16:8 and before the longer ending; one Latin manuscript has it alone. Its words and style are not Mark's, and it seems written to round off a Gospel that ended at 16:8. It contradicts 16:8, where the women say nothing to anyone. See the notes on 16:8. It is translated here in square brackets: the opening bracket at the start of this ending and the closing bracket after its last word, "Amen", mark where it begins and ends. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

records.literal_gloss: After now these things also himself the Jesus from east and as far as west sent out through them the holy and imperishable proclamation of the eternal salvation.

en.L: And after these things Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} also sent out through them, from [the] east even to [the] west, the holy and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation.
en.B: After this Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} sent out through them, from east to west, the sacred and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation.
en.R: After that, Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} used them to send out the holy message of eternal salvation from the east to the west. It is a message that will never pass away.

vi.L: Sau đó, chính Đức Giê-xu cũng qua họ mà sai truyền từ phương đông cho đến phương tây lời rao giảng thánh và bất diệt về sự cứu rỗi đời đời.
vi.B: Sau đó, chính Đức Giê-xu qua họ đã truyền đi từ đông sang tây lời rao giảng thánh và bất diệt về sự cứu rỗi đời đời.
vi.R: Sau đó, chính Đức Giê-xu dùng họ để truyền đi sứ điệp thánh về sự cứu rỗi đời đời, từ phương đông đến phương tây. Đó là sứ điệp sẽ không bao giờ mất đi.

ko.L: 그리고 이 일들 후에 예수께서 친히 그들을 통하여 동쪽에서부터 서쪽까지, 영원한 구원에 대한 거룩하고 썩지 않는 선포를 내보내셨다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 예수께서 친히 그들을 통하여, 해 뜨는 곳에서 해 지는 곳까지 영원한 구원을 알리는 거룩하고 썩지 않는 선포를 내보내셨다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 예수께서 직접 그들을 보내셔서, 동쪽 끝에서 서쪽 끝까지 영원한 구원의 거룩한 소식을 전하게 하셨다. 그 소식은 결코 없어지지 않는다.

es.L: Y después de esto, también Jesús mismo envió por medio de ellos, desde [el] oriente hasta [el] occidente, la santa e incorruptible proclamación de la salvación eterna.
es.B: Después de esto, Jesús mismo envió por medio de ellos, de oriente a occidente, la proclamación sagrada e imperecedera de la salvación eterna.
es.R: Después de eso, Jesús mismo los usó para enviar el santo mensaje de la salvación eterna desde el oriente hasta el occidente. Es un mensaje que nunca dejará de existir.

fr.L: Et après cela, Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} envoya aussi par eux, du levant jusqu’au couchant, la proclamation sainte et impérissable du salut éternel.
fr.B: Après cela, Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} envoya par eux, de l’orient à l’occident, la proclamation sacrée et impérissable du salut éternel.
fr.R: Après cela, Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} s’est servi d’eux pour envoyer, de l’est jusqu’à l’ouest, le message saint du salut éternel. C’est un message qui ne disparaîtra jamais.

sw.L: Na baada ya mambo haya Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} pia alipeleka kupitia wao, kutoka mashariki hata magharibi, tangazo takatifu lisiloharibika la wokovu wa milele.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alituma kupitia wao, kutoka mashariki hadi magharibi, ujumbe mtakatifu usioharibika wa wokovu wa milele.
sw.R: Baadaye Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} aliwatumia wao kupeleka ujumbe mtakatifu wa wokovu wa milele kutoka mashariki hadi magharibi. Ni ujumbe ambao hautapita kamwe.

pt.L: E, depois disso, o próprio Jesus também enviou por meio deles, do oriente até o ocidente, a santa e incorruptível proclamação da salvação eterna.
pt.B: Depois disso, o próprio Jesus enviou por meio deles, do oriente ao ocidente, a sagrada e imperecível proclamação da salvação eterna.
pt.R: Depois disso, o próprio Jesus usou essas pessoas para enviar a santa mensagem da salvação eterna desde o oriente até o ocidente. É uma mensagem que nunca vai passar.

decisions.choice: from east to west: through the whole world
decisions.reason: The rising and setting of the sun stand for the whole earth (Psalm 113:3; Malachi 1:11).

decisions.choice: imperishable: that cannot decay or die
decisions.reason: The word is used of God (Romans 1:23) and of the resurrection body (1 Corinthians 15:52). The message is undying.

decisions.choice: proclamation: the message preached, the announcement of Jesus
decisions.reason: The word names the content of what was preached, as in 1 Corinthians 1:21.

decisions.choice: eternal salvation: rescue that lasts forever
decisions.reason: The phrase is found in Hebrews 5:9. It is not a phrase Mark uses, which is one sign that this ending comes from a later hand.

decisions.choice: a message that will never pass away
decisions.reason: Readable explains "imperishable" in a separate sentence and uses "message" for the proclamation.

decisions.choice: "sự cứu rỗi" for salvation, every level
decisions.reason: The Protestant word for salvation, as in John 4:22.

decisions.choice: "chính Đức Giê-xu" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks "Jesus himself" with "chính" before the name, with no pronoun, so the English span on "himself" has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: "선포" (L, B), "소식" (R) for kerygma; "썩지 않는" (L, B), "결코 없어지지 않는" (R) for aphthartos
decisions.reason: "선포" keeps the act of proclaiming that the word names; "썩지 않는" is the Korean for what cannot decay (meaning decision), and Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: "해 뜨는 곳에서 해 지는 곳까지" (B)
decisions.reason: The Korean idiom for the whole world from end to end, which is what the phrase means (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: incorruptible (L); imperecedera (B); que nunca dejará de existir (R); proclamación (L, B); mensaje (R)
decisions.reason: "Proclamación" is the message announced (meaning decision m3); Readable says "mensaje". The adjective means that it cannot decay or die (meaning decision m2). "Jesús mismo" has no pronoun, so it takes no setting.

decisions.choice: la proclamation (L, B); le message (R); le salut éternel (every level)
decisions.reason: "Proclamation" is the announcement itself (meaning decision m3); "prédication" would suggest a sermon in church, and "kérygme" is a specialist word. "Salut" is the French key term for salvation, kept at every level.

decisions.choice: tangazo (L); ujumbe (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is the message proclaimed (meaning decision). Literal says "tangazo" (proclamation); Balanced and Readable say "ujumbe" (message), which reads naturally with "sent out". "Injili" is kept for the noun gospel.

decisions.choice: o próprio Jesus, with no setting
decisions.reason: The English "Jesus himself" puts the reflexive under the setting. Portuguese says "o próprio Jesus", an adjective rather than a pronoun, so there is no pronoun to capitalise and no span.

decisions.choice: "ስብከት" (preaching) (L), "አዋጅ" (proclamation) (B), "መልእክት" (message) (R); "መዳን" (salvation)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the message as it is announced, not the word for gospel; Literal and Balanced keep the act of proclaiming, Readable the message itself, as the English does.

en.B: [After {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had risen, early in the morning of the first day of the week, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} first to Mary Magdalene. It was from her that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had thrown out seven demons.

ko.L: [그런데 주간의 첫 [날] 이른 아침에 살아나신 그분은, 전에 일곱 귀신을 쫓아내 주셨던 막달라 마리아에게 먼저 나타나셨다.

fr.L: [Or, étant ressuscité de bon matin, le premier [jour] de la semaine, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} apparut d’abord à Marie de Magdala, de laquelle {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait chassé sept démons.

sw.L: [Basi alipokwisha kufufuka mapema siku ya kwanza ya juma, alimtokea kwanza Mariamu Magdalene, ambaye alikuwa amemtoa pepo saba.

decisions.choice: 16:9-20, the longer ending: found in most manuscripts but not in the earliest; printed by the SBLGNT in double brackets
decisions.reason: The two oldest complete manuscripts of the New Testament, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, both from the fourth century, end Mark at 16:8 with "for they were afraid". Most manuscripts, nearly all of them later, go on with 16:9-20, the longer ending. Its style and vocabulary differ from the rest of Mark: many of its words occur nowhere else in the Gospel, it introduces Mary Magdalene in 16:9 as if she had not just been named in 16:1, and its appearances read like a summary of those told in Luke, John and Acts. Some manuscripts have instead a short ending after 16:8 (the women report briefly to Peter's companions, and Jesus sends out through them the proclamation of eternal salvation), and a few have the short ending followed by the longer one. The SBLGNT prints both endings after 16:8 in double brackets, which mark a passage that was not part of the original text but is old and widely read. It is translated here in square brackets: the opening bracket at the start of 16:9 and the closing bracket at the end of 16:20 mark where the passage begins and ends. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: an open question: Mark may have ended at 16:8 on purpose, or his ending may have been lost
decisions.reason: Whether Mark meant to end at 16:8 or his first ending was lost is an open question. A book ending on the word "for", with the women silent and afraid, is very unusual, and it leaves the meeting promised in 16:7 untold. Some think the last page of the earliest copy was lost or never written. Others think Mark ended here on purpose: the promise of 16:7 stands, the reader knows the message was later told, and the silence leaves the reader facing the empty tomb. The later endings show that early copyists felt the Gospel needed a fuller close. The manuscripts cannot settle the question. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

records.literal_gloss: She having gone told [it] to those with him having been, mourning and weeping;

en.L: She went and told [it] to those who had been with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, as they were mourning and weeping;
en.B: She went and brought the news to the people who had been with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, who were grieving and weeping.

ko.L: 그 여자가 가서, 그분과 함께 있던 사람들, 곧 슬퍼하며 울고 있던 사람들에게 알렸다.

ko.R: 마리아는 가서 예수와 함께 다니던 사람들에게 이 일을 알렸다. 그들은 몹시 슬퍼하며 울고 있었다.

es.L: Ella fue y [lo] anunció a los que habían estado con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, que estaban de luto y llorando.
es.B: Ella fue a dar la noticia a los que habían estado con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, que estaban de duelo y llorando.
es.R: Ella fue y se lo contó a los que habían estado con Jesús. Estaban muy tristes y lloraban.

fr.L: Celle-là alla l’annoncer à ceux qui avaient été avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, qui étaient dans le deuil et pleuraient ;
fr.B: Elle alla porter la nouvelle à ceux qui avaient été avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et qui étaient dans le deuil et en larmes.
fr.R: Elle est allée le dire à ceux qui avaient été avec Jésus. Ils étaient très tristes et ils pleuraient.

sw.B: Alikwenda, akawapelekea habari wale waliokuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, ambao walikuwa wakiomboleza na kulia.
sw.R: Mariamu alikwenda akawaambia watu waliokuwa pamoja na Yesu. Walikuwa na huzuni nyingi na walikuwa wakilia.

pt.L: Ela foi e anunciou [isso] aos que tinham estado com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, enquanto estavam de luto e chorando;
pt.B: Ela foi e levou a notícia aos que tinham estado com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, que estavam de luto e chorando.
pt.R: Ela foi e contou isso às pessoas que tinham estado com Jesus. Elas estavam muito tristes e chorando.

decisions.choice: those who had been with him: his disciples and close followers
decisions.reason: The phrase is wider than the eleven, though it includes them (3:14).

decisions.choice: mourning and weeping: grieving aloud for the dead
decisions.reason: The two words describe open grief, the mourning for the dead that was customary.

decisions.choice: the people who had been with Jesus
alternatives: those who had been with him
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus, since the pronoun alone could be unclear.

decisions.choice: de luto (L); de duelo (B); muy tristes (R)
decisions.reason: Mourning aloud for the dead (meaning decision m2); Readable uses everyday words. The stressed "él" for Jesus takes the setting; Readable names him.

records.literal_gloss: And they having heard that he lives and was seen by her disbelieved.

en.L: And they, hearing that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was alive and had been seen by her, disbelieved.
en.B: But on hearing that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was alive and that she had seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they would not believe it.
en.R: The followers heard that Jesus was alive and that Mary had seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But they did not believe her.

vi.R: Những người ấy nghe nói Đức Giê-xu đang sống và Ma-ri đã thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Nhưng họ không tin bà.

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 그분이 살아 계시고 그 여자에게 보이셨다는 것을 듣고도 믿지 않았다.

ko.R: 그 사람들은 예수께서 살아 계시고 마리아가 예수를 뵈었다는 말을 들었다. 그러나 마리아의 말을 믿지 않았다.

es.L: Y ellos, al oír que vivía y que había sido visto por ella, no [lo] creyeron.
es.B: Pero cuando oyeron que estaba vivo y que ella {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había visto, no lo quisieron creer.
es.R: Los discípulos oyeron que Jesús estaba vivo y que María {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había visto. Pero no le creyeron.

fr.B: Mais quand ils entendirent qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était vivant et qu’elle {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avait vu, ils refusèrent de le croire.
fr.R: Ils ont appris que Jésus était vivant et que Marie {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avait vu. Mais ils ne l’ont pas crue.

sw.L: Nao waliposikia kwamba yu hai na kwamba ameonwa naye, hawakuamini.
sw.B: Lakini waliposikia kwamba yu hai na kwamba Mariamu alikuwa amemwona, hawakukubali kuamini.
sw.R: Watu hao walisikia kwamba Yesu yu hai na kwamba Mariamu alikuwa amemwona. Lakini hawakumwamini.

pt.L: E eles, ouvindo que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava vivo e que tinha sido visto por ela, não creram.
pt.B: Mas, ao ouvirem que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava vivo e que ela {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} tinha visto, não quiseram crer.
pt.R: Os seguidores ouviram que Jesus estava vivo e que Maria {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} tinha visto. Mas não acreditaram nela.
